note: Dhivehi Quiz questions (English). a[0] is the right answer; the game shuffles. checked:false = not yet reviewed by the owner.

q.q: In which year did the Maldives gain independence from the United Kingdom?
q.f: Independence Day is marked every year on 26 July.

q.q: Who was the first President of the Maldives, in the short-lived republic of 1953?
q.f: That first republic lasted less than a year before the sultanate returned.

q.q: According to Maldivian tradition, in which year did the islands convert to Islam?
q.f: Before Islam, many islanders followed Buddhism.

q.q: Before Islam, which religion was widely followed in the Maldives?
q.f: Ruins of Buddhist stupas and monasteries have been found on several islands.

q.q: Which national hero led the fight that ended the Portuguese occupation of Malé in 1573?
q.f: National Day, on the first of Rabi' al-Awwal, marks this victory.

q.q: Which European power occupied Malé in the 1500s?
q.f: The occupation ended in 1573.

q.q: In which year did the Maldives become a British protected state?
q.f: Britain handled foreign affairs, while the sultans ran the country at home.

q.q: The Maldives' first written constitution came in which year?
q.f: It was introduced under Sultan Muhammad Shamsuddeen III.

q.q: Who was the first President of the Second Republic, from 1968?
q.f: He had been Prime Minister before the sultanate ended.

q.q: Who was President of the Maldives from 1978 to 2008?
q.f: His 30 years in office made him one of Asia's longest-serving leaders.

q.q: Who won the Maldives' first multi-party presidential election, in 2008?
q.f: A new constitution adopted in 2008 opened the way for multi-party elections.

q.q: In which year did the Indian Ocean tsunami strike the Maldives?
q.f: The waves came on 26 December and flooded many low-lying islands.

q.q: The Maldives joined the United Nations in which year?
q.f: It joined in September 1965, just weeks after independence.

q.q: Which island in Addu Atoll was a British Royal Air Force base until 1976?
q.f: The old runway on Gan is still used today as Gan International Airport.

q.q: Which famous Moroccan traveller lived in the Maldives in the 1340s and served as a judge?
q.f: He wrote about the islands, their cowrie shells and their coconut-fibre rope.

q.q: Malé's Old Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy) is famous for walls made of what?
q.f: It was built in 1658, and its coral blocks are finely carved.

q.q: Which shells from the Maldives were once used as money across Asia and Africa?
q.f: Ships carried Maldivian cowries as far as West Africa.

q.q: In 1988, troops from which country helped stop an attempted coup in Malé?
q.f: The day it was defeated, 3 November, is marked as Victory Day.

q.q: What was the name of Muhammad Thakurufaanu's famous boat?
q.f: After the victory over the Portuguese, he ruled the Maldives as Sultan.

q.q: Muhammad Thakurufaanu came from which island?
q.f: His family home, Utheemu Ganduvaru, is a wooden palace kept as a museum.

q.q: The sultanate ended and the Second Republic began in which year?
q.f: The republic began on 11 November 1968, now marked as Republic Day.

q.q: In which park in Malé does the National Museum stand?
q.f: The park was once part of the grounds of the sultans' palace.

q.q: What is the name of the President's official residence in Malé?
q.f: It was built in the early 1900s, near the Old Friday Mosque.

q.q: The Lōmāfānu, the oldest known Maldivian documents, were written on plates of which metal?
q.f: They date from the late 1100s and use the old Dhives Akuru script.

q.q: What was the first tourist resort in the Maldives, opened in 1972?
q.f: Kurumba is the Dhivehi word for a young coconut.

q.q: What is the capital city of the Maldives?
q.f: Malé is among the most densely populated cities in the world.

q.q: Which is the southernmost atoll of the Maldives?
q.f: Addu Atoll lies just south of the equator.

q.q: Which administrative atoll is the northernmost in the Maldives?
q.f: Its island Utheemu was the home of Muhammad Thakurufaanu.

q.q: The Maldives is made up of how many natural atolls?
q.f: For government, they are grouped into 20 administrative atolls with Thaana letter names.

q.q: Which island is an atoll all on its own?
q.f: Fuvahmulah is also known for its freshwater lakes, rare in the Maldives.

q.q: Which island next to Malé was built by land reclamation, starting in 1997?
q.f: It was built to give the crowded capital room to grow.

q.q: Thilafushi, near Malé, is best known as what?
a: An island made for the capital's rubbish
q.f: It was created in the early 1990s by filling in a lagoon.

q.q: The main international airport, Velana International, is on which island?
q.f: Seaplanes to the resorts take off from a lagoon beside the airport.

q.q: The Sinamalé Bridge, opened in 2018, links Malé with which island?
q.f: It is also called the China–Maldives Friendship Bridge.

q.q: The Maldives is often called the world's what?
q.f: Most of its islands are only a metre or two above sea level.

q.q: The English word 'atoll' comes from which language?
q.f: It comes from the Dhivehi word 'atholhu'.

q.q: Which imaginary line passes through the southern Maldives?
q.f: The Equatorial Channel lies between Huvadhu Atoll and Fuvahmulah.

q.q: Huvadhu Atoll is split into which two administrative atolls?
q.f: Huvadhu is one of the largest atolls in the world.

q.q: Malé lies in which atoll?
q.f: Kaafu is also home to many of the oldest resorts.

q.q: Ari Atoll is split into which administrative atolls?
q.f: South Ari Atoll is famous for whale sharks.

q.q: Hithadhoo is the main island of which city?
q.f: Addu City covers several islands of Addu Atoll.

q.q: In Addu City, a road over causeways links Hithadhoo, Maradhoo, Feydhoo and which island?
q.f: The road is often called the Link Road.

q.q: Kulhudhuffushi City is in which atoll?
q.f: It is a busy hub for the northern atolls.

q.q: Thinadhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Thinadhoo lies in the southern half of Huvadhu Atoll.

q.q: Which island near Malé was a tourist resort before it became part of the capital?
q.f: Today it is known as Villimalé, a quiet district a short ferry ride from Malé.

q.q: Roughly how many coral islands make up the Maldives?
q.f: Fewer than 200 of them have local communities.

q.q: The One and a Half Degree Channel separates Huvadhu Atoll from which atoll?
q.f: It is named after its latitude, about 1.5 degrees north of the equator.

q.q: The Maldives lies in which ocean?
q.f: It sits south-west of India and Sri Lanka.

q.q: Which two countries are the Maldives' nearest neighbours?
q.f: Minicoy, an Indian island just north of the Maldives, speaks a form of Dhivehi.

q.q: Addu Atoll is also known by which Thaana letter name?
q.f: Gnaviyani is the letter name used for Fuvahmulah.

q.q: In which direction is Thaana written?
q.f: Like Arabic, Thaana runs from right to left.

q.q: Which letter comes first in the Thaana alphabet?
q.f: The first nine Thaana letters, haa to vaavu, were shaped from Arabic numerals.

q.q: How many basic letters does the Thaana alphabet have?
q.f: Extra dotted letters, called thikijehi thaana, are used for Arabic words.

q.q: What are the vowel marks written above or below Thaana letters called?
q.f: In Thaana, vowels are written as fili, not as separate letters.

q.q: Dhivehi is most closely related to which language?
q.f: Both belong to the Indo-Aryan family of languages.

q.q: What was the older Maldivian script, used before Thaana?
q.f: It was written from left to right, unlike Thaana.

q.q: Which Thaana letter carries the vowel at the start of a word like 'atholhu'?
q.f: On its own alifu is silent: the fili on it gives the sound.

q.q: The word 'Dhivehi' comes from 'dhivehin'. What does 'dhivehin' mean?
q.f: So 'Dhivehi' is the language of the islanders.

q.q: What is the number 'three' in Dhivehi?
q.f: One, two, three in Dhivehi: ekeh, dheyh, thineh.

q.q: The card game Dhihaeh is named after a number. Which one?
q.f: In Dhihaeh, teams try to capture the four tens.

q.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Dhivehi?
q.f: 'Aan' means yes, and 'noon' means no.

q.q: 'Haalu kihineh?' is a common way to ask what?
q.f: 'Kihineh' on its own means 'how?'.

q.q: What does 'varah reethi' mean?
q.f: 'Reethi' means beautiful, and 'varah' means very.

q.q: What does 'fen' mean in Dhivehi?
q.f: Fish is 'mas' and rice is 'bath'.

q.q: Which Dhivehi word means 'fish'?
q.f: That is why tuna dishes have names like mas huni and mas riha.

q.q: Many island names end in '-dhoo', like Hithadhoo. What does 'dhoo' mean?
q.f: Many other names end in '-fushi', another word for an island.

q.q: What do Maldivians call their country in Dhivehi?
q.f: 'Raajje' on its own is often used to mean the whole country.

q.q: Which day of the week is 'Hukuru'?
q.f: The Old Friday Mosque in Malé is called Hukuru Miskiy.

q.q: What does a sukun on a Thaana letter show?
a: That no vowel follows the letter
That the word is a name
q.f: The sukun is drawn as a small circle above the letter.

q.q: What is the official language of the Maldives?
q.f: English is also widely used, especially in schools and business.

q.q: How is the word 'Dhivehi' written in Thaana?
q.f: Read it from right to left: dhi, ve, hi.

q.q: Which letter comes second in the Thaana alphabet?
q.f: The alphabet begins haa, shaviyani, noonu, raa, baa.

q.q: The administrative atolls are named after Thaana letters. How are the letters ordered?
a: In alphabet order, from north to south
In alphabet order, from south to north
q.f: Haa Alifu, in the far north, starts with the first letter, haa.

q.q: What does 'bodu' mean, as in 'bodu beru'?
q.f: Bodu beru means 'big drum'.

q.q: What does 'kuda' mean, as in the island name Kuda Huraa?
q.f: Its opposite is 'bodu', meaning big, as in nearby Bodu Huraa.

q.q: Garudhiya is a clear broth made mainly from what?
q.f: It is usually eaten with rice, lime, chilli and onion.

q.q: Mas huni is traditionally eaten with which flatbread?
q.f: Mas huni mixes tuna, grated coconut, onion and chilli.

q.q: What are 'hedhikaa'?
q.f: Short eats like gulha and bajiya are hedhikaa, often served in the afternoon.

q.q: Bis keemiya is a pastry usually filled with egg, onion and which vegetable?
q.f: 'Bis' is the Dhivehi word for egg.

q.q: What is masroshi?
a: Roshi dough filled with a tuna mix and baked
q.f: The filling is usually mas huni.

q.q: Gulha are small fried balls filled with what?
a: A tuna, coconut and onion mix
q.f: They are one of the best-loved hedhikaa.

q.q: Rihaakuru is a thick paste made by cooking down what?
q.f: It is salty and strong, so a little goes a long way with rice.

q.q: What is valhoamas?
q.f: Smoking was a traditional way to keep fish for a long time.

q.q: The hard, cured tuna known abroad as 'Maldive fish' is called what in Dhivehi?
q.f: It was traded to Sri Lanka and India for centuries.

q.q: Bondibaiy is a sweet dish made mainly from what?
q.f: The rice is cooked with coconut milk and sugar.

q.q: Bajiya is best described as what?
a: A fried pastry, usually with a tuna filling
q.f: It looks a lot like a samosa.

q.q: 'Theluli mas' is fish cooked how?
q.f: 'Theluli' means fried in Dhivehi.

q.q: What is mas riha?
q.f: It is usually made with tuna and eaten with rice or roshi.

q.q: What is a 'kurumba'?
q.f: Its water is a favourite cool drink.

q.q: Raa, a traditional sweet drink, is sap from which tree?
q.f: The person who climbs the palm to collect it is called a raaveriyaa.

q.q: Dhiyaa hakuru is a syrup made by boiling down what?
q.f: 'Hakuru' means sugar in Dhivehi.

q.q: What is 'bambukeyo'?
q.f: It is often boiled, fried as chips or cooked in a curry.

q.q: Fihunu mas is fish cooked how?
q.f: It is often rubbed with a chilli paste before grilling.

q.q: Which fish is the most important in Maldivian fishing and cooking?
q.f: In Dhivehi it is called kalhubilamas.

q.q: What is 'kaashi'?
q.f: Grated coconut goes into many dishes, from mas huni to sweets.

q.q: Saagu bondibaiy is a pudding made with sago and which milk?
q.f: Sago pearls turn clear when they are cooked.

q.q: What is 'githeyo mirus'?
q.f: 'Mirus' means chilli in Dhivehi.

q.q: 'Kalhu sai' is what drink?
q.f: 'Kalhu' means black, and 'sai' means tea.

q.q: After a meal, many older Maldivians chew 'foah' and 'bileh'. What are they?
q.f: The pair is often offered to guests.

q.q: In 'mas huni', what does 'huni' mean?
q.f: 'Mas' means fish, so mas huni is fish with grated coconut.

q.q: Hanifaru Bay, famous for gatherings of manta rays, is in which atoll?
q.f: Hanifaru is part of the Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

q.q: What is the largest fish in the sea, often seen in South Ari Atoll?
q.f: Whale sharks are filter feeders: they eat plankton.

q.q: How is Maldivian tuna famously caught?
a: One by one, with pole and line
q.f: Catching fish one at a time means very few other animals are caught by mistake.

q.q: What is the traditional Maldivian boat called?
q.f: A 'masdhoni' is a dhoni used for fishing.

q.q: Which two sea turtles are most often seen on Maldivian reefs?
q.f: Five species of sea turtle have been recorded in Maldivian waters.

q.q: In which year did a strong El Niño cause mass coral bleaching across the Maldives?
q.f: Another big bleaching event hit the reefs in 2016.

q.q: The Maldives banned all shark fishing in which year?
q.f: Divers come from around the world to see sharks on Maldivian reefs.

q.q: The Maldives has the world's largest known population of which ray?
q.f: Each manta has its own pattern of spots on its belly, like a fingerprint.

q.q: Much of the white sand on Maldivian beaches is made by which fish?
q.f: Parrotfish bite off bits of coral, grind them up and pass out fine sand.

q.q: Clownfish live among the stinging tentacles of what?
q.f: One species is called the Maldive anemonefish.

q.q: The humphead wrasse is also known by which name?
q.f: It can grow to about two metres long.

q.q: What makes some Maldivian beaches glow blue at night?
q.f: The plankton light up when waves disturb them.

q.q: Which dolphin, famous for leaping and spinning in the air, is often seen in the Maldives?
q.f: They often travel in large groups, called pods.

q.q: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called what?
q.f: Each polyp builds a hard limestone skeleton around itself.

q.q: Scientists explain that an atoll forms when coral grows around what?
q.f: As the island sinks, the reef keeps growing up, leaving a ring around a lagoon.

q.q: What is 'kanneli' in English?
q.f: Yellowfin grow much bigger than skipjack.

q.q: Alimatha in Vaavu Atoll is famous for night dives with which sharks?
q.f: Nurse sharks are mostly calm and often rest on the sea floor.

q.q: Early-morning divers off Rasdhoo in Ari Atoll hope to see which sharks?
q.f: Hammerheads have wide heads with an eye at each end.

q.q: Which starfish is a pest on reefs because it eats coral?
q.f: Its body is covered in sharp, venomous spines.

q.q: Which small shark is often seen in shallow lagoons, with dark tips on its fins?
q.f: Young blacktips often swim in very shallow water near the beach.

q.q: The long spines of a lionfish are what?
q.f: Look but never touch: a sting is very painful.

q.q: Which fish looks like a rock and has very venomous spines?
q.f: It is one of the most venomous fish in the world, so reef shoes help.

q.q: Which sea animal squirts ink to escape danger?
q.f: Octopuses can also change colour to hide.

q.q: What kind of animal is a moray?
q.f: Morays open and close their mouths to breathe; it is not a threat.

q.q: What are the tiny algae that live inside coral and give it colour called?
q.f: In water that is too warm, coral pushes them out and turns white: this is bleaching.

q.q: The Maldives won the SAFF Championship in 2008. In which year did they win it again?
q.f: Both titles were won in finals against India.

q.q: What is the most popular sport in the Maldives?
q.f: Big matches at the National Football Stadium in Malé draw large crowds.

q.q: In the traditional women's game bashi, how does the server hit the ball?
a: Backwards over her head, facing away from the net
q.f: Bashi is played with a racket and a tennis ball.

q.q: The National Football Stadium is in which district of Malé?
q.f: It is often called the Galolhu Stadium.

q.q: In which year did the Maldives first take part in the Olympic Games?
q.f: Those Games were held in Seoul, South Korea.

q.q: The famous surf break 'Cokes' is off which island?
q.f: It is named after the Coca-Cola bottling plant on the island.

q.q: Which board game, played by flicking a striker at small discs, is hugely popular in the Maldives?
q.f: Carrom boards are a common sight at homes and in cafés.

q.q: In carrom, what is the red piece called?
q.f: Pocket the queen and you must 'cover' it by pocketing one of your own pieces next.

q.q: How many players does a football team have on the pitch?
q.f: One of the eleven is the goalkeeper.

q.q: How long is a normal football match, not counting stoppage time?
q.f: It is played in two halves of 45 minutes.

q.q: How many players does a volleyball team have on the court?
q.f: Beach volleyball is played two a side.

q.q: In badminton, a standard game is won by the first side to reach how many points?
q.f: At 20 all, a side must lead by two, up to a limit of 30.

q.q: In tennis, what does the score 'love' mean?
q.f: A tie at 40 all is called deuce.

q.q: How often is the men's FIFA World Cup held?
q.f: The first World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930.

q.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
q.f: The rings stand for five parts of the world coming together.

q.q: In cricket, how many balls make up an over?
q.f: No bowler may bowl two overs in a row.

q.q: How long is a marathon?
q.f: A half marathon is about 21.1 km.

q.q: What does SCUBA stand for?
q.f: Divers breathe compressed air from a tank on their back.

q.q: Which swimming stroke is usually the fastest?
q.f: In freestyle races almost everyone swims front crawl.

q.q: In which sport do players 'spike' and 'block' at the net?
q.f: A team may touch the ball up to three times before sending it over.

q.q: Which sport is played at Wimbledon?
q.f: It is played on grass courts in London.

q.q: In football, what is it called when one player scores three goals in a match?
q.f: Cricket uses the same word for three wickets from three balls in a row.

q.q: In golf, what is one stroke under par on a hole called?
q.f: Two under par is an eagle.

q.q: How many players does a basketball team have on the court?
q.f: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith.

q.q: Which chess piece can only move diagonally?
q.f: Each bishop stays on squares of one colour for the whole game.

q.q: What is bodu beru?
q.f: Bodu beru means “big drum”.

q.q: In the dance bandiyaa jehun, what do the dancers tap in time with the music?
q.f: The dance is performed by women, usually in a group.

q.q: What do the dancers hold in dhandi jehun?
q.f: 'Dhandi' means stick in Dhivehi.

q.q: What is raivaru?
a: A traditional form of sung poetry
q.f: It is one of the oldest forms of Maldivian poetry.

q.q: The Dhivehi libaas, a traditional dress, is known for what?
q.f: The gold embroidery around the neck is called kasabu.

q.q: Thulhaadhoo in Baa Atoll is famous for which craft?
q.f: Craftsmen turn wood and layer it with coloured lacquer.

q.q: Thundu kunaa, the finest woven mats, come from which atoll?
q.f: Weaving one takes great skill and a lot of time.

q.q: On which date is Independence Day celebrated?
q.f: It marks independence from Britain in 1965.

q.q: Republic Day in the Maldives falls on which date?
q.f: It marks the start of the Second Republic in 1968.

q.q: Which date is Victory Day, remembering the defeat of the 1988 coup attempt?
q.f: The government asked India for help, and troops arrived within hours.

q.q: What is in the green centre of the Maldivian flag?
q.f: The red border is said to stand for the blood of national heroes.

q.q: What is the national anthem of the Maldives called?
q.f: Its present tune was composed in 1972 by the Sri Lankan musician W. D. Amaradeva.

q.q: In the performance called thaara, men sit in rows and play what?
q.f: The word thaara is also the name of the drum.

q.q: In the Maldives, Eid al-Fitr, at the end of Ramadan, is known as what?
q.f: Eid al-Adha is called Bodu Eid, the 'big Eid'.

q.q: Maahefun is a celebration held just before what?
q.f: Families gather for a big meal before the fast begins.

q.q: Which Disney film follows a girl chosen by the ocean on a voyage across the Pacific?
q.f: Moana was released in 2016.

q.q: In 'Finding Nemo', what kind of fish is Nemo?
q.f: His friend Dory is a blue tang.

q.q: Where does SpongeBob SquarePants live?
a: In a pineapple under the sea
q.f: His town is called Bikini Bottom.

q.q: Which band sang 'Yellow Submarine'?
q.f: The Beatles came from Liverpool, England.

q.q: Digu, the favourite Maldivian card game, is a kind of what?
q.f: Players make sets and runs, as in gin rummy.

q.q: In the card game Bondi, what is the last player still holding cards called?
q.f: Bondi is played with one 52-card deck, by 2 to 5 players.

q.q: Which two days make up the weekend in the Maldives?
q.f: Friday is the day of the main weekly prayer.

q.q: In 'Frozen', who sings 'Let It Go'?
q.f: Elsa has the power to make ice and snow.

q.q: What is a feyli?
q.f: It was traditionally woven by hand on a loom.

q.q: What is the big square by Malé's waterfront, used for national events, called?
q.f: The national flag flies over the square.

q.q: What is the currency of the Maldives?
q.f: One rufiyaa is 100 laari.

q.q: What is the national bird of the Maldives?
q.f: In Dhivehi it is called kanbili.

q.q: What is the national tree of the Maldives?
q.f: A coconut palm also appears on the national emblem.

q.q: What is the national flower of the Maldives?
q.f: The coconut palm and the pink rose are both national symbols.

q.q: Which time zone does the Maldives use?
q.f: Some resorts set their clocks an hour ahead, on 'island time'.

q.q: What is the international calling code of the Maldives?
q.f: +94 is Sri Lanka and +91 is India.

q.q: Which internet domain ending belongs to the Maldives?
q.f: .md is Moldova and .ml is Mali.

q.q: What is the Maldivian parliament called?
q.f: 'Majlis' is a word for a council or assembly.

q.q: On which side of the road do vehicles drive in the Maldives?
q.f: It is the same as in India and Sri Lanka.

q.q: The Maldives is a founding member of which South Asian regional group?
q.f: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985.

q.q: Which Maldivian city hosted the SAARC summit in 2011?
q.f: It was the 17th SAARC summit.

q.q: What is the three-letter currency code of the rufiyaa?
q.f: Prices are often written with 'Rf' or 'MVR'.

q.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
q.f: The Indian Ocean, home of the Maldives, is the third largest.

q.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
q.f: Iron-rich dust gives Mars its reddish colour.

q.q: How many continents are there, by the most common count?
q.f: Asia is the largest continent.

q.q: Which gas do plants take in from the air to make their food?
q.f: They give off oxygen as they do it.

q.q: How many days are in a leap year?
q.f: February gets an extra day, the 29th.

q.q: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
q.f: Jupiter is more than 11 times wider than Earth.

q.q: At sea level, water boils at what temperature?
q.f: That is 212 degrees Fahrenheit.

q.q: What is the largest animal on Earth?
q.f: The whale shark is the largest fish, but the blue whale is a mammal.

q.q: What is the capital of India?
q.f: India is the Maldives' biggest neighbour.

q.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
q.f: It was once widely used in thermometers.

q.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
q.f: It hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.

q.q: What is the hardest natural material?
q.f: Diamond is a form of pure carbon.

q.q: How many legs does a spider have?
q.f: Insects have six legs, so spiders are not insects.

q.q: Which sultan built Malé's Old Friday Mosque (Hukuru Miskiy) in 1658?
q.f: He also built the round minaret beside it, the Munnaaru.

q.q: Who was President when the new constitution of 2008 was ratified?
q.f: Mohamed Nasheed took office later that year, in November 2008.

q.q: In which year did President Mohamed Nasheed resign?
q.f: His vice-president, Mohamed Waheed, then became President.

q.q: Who was elected President of the Maldives in 2013?
q.f: He served until 2018.

q.q: Who won the Maldives' presidential election in 2018?
q.f: He took office on 17 November 2018.

q.q: The Huraa dynasty, the last royal family of the Maldives, ruled until which year?
q.f: The dynasty takes its name from the island of Huraa in Kaafu Atoll.

q.q: Who was the last Sultan of the Maldives?
q.f: After independence in 1965 he was styled King, until the republic of 1968.

q.q: The breakaway United Suvadive Republic (1959–1963) was formed by Addu, Huvadhu and which other southern atoll?
q.f: Its president, Abdullah Afeef, later lived in exile in the Seychelles.

q.q: Before it was renamed Velana in 2017, the main airport was named after which former President?
q.f: The airport on Hulhulé first opened in 1966.

q.q: Majeediyya School, one of the oldest modern schools in Malé, opened in which year?
q.f: Many of the country's leaders went to school there.

q.q: Muhammad Thakurufaanu founded which royal dynasty?
q.f: It is named after his home island, Utheemu in Haa Alifu.

q.q: In the Second World War, Addu Atoll was a secret British naval base known by what code name?
q.f: Its deep, sheltered lagoon gave warships a safe anchorage.

q.q: The Maldives left the Commonwealth in 2016. In which year did it rejoin?
q.f: The Commonwealth is a group of more than 50 countries, most once linked to Britain.

q.q: Eydhafushi is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: The whole of Baa Atoll is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

q.q: Naifaru is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Lhaviyani Atoll is also called Faadhippolhu.

q.q: Rasdhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Rasdhoo sits on its own small atoll, at the north-east edge of Ari.

q.q: Funadhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Shaviyani is the second letter of the Thaana alphabet.

q.q: Manadhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Noonu is the third letter of the Thaana alphabet.

q.q: Ungoofaaru is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Raa is the fourth letter of the Thaana alphabet.

q.q: Mahibadhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Alifu Dhaalu covers the southern part of Ari Atoll.

q.q: Felidhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Vaavu is also home to Alimatha, famous for night dives.

q.q: Kudahuvadhoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Dhaalu Atoll is also called South Nilandhe Atoll.

q.q: Veymandoo is the capital island of which atoll?
q.f: Thaa Atoll is also called Kolhumadulu.

q.q: Hanimaadhoo, with an airport for the far north, is in which atoll?
q.f: Haa Dhaalu is also home to Kulhudhuffushi City.

q.q: Kadhdhoo airport serves which atoll?
q.f: Laamu Atoll is also called Hadhdhunmathi.

q.q: Kaadedhdhoo airport, near Thinadhoo, is in which atoll?
q.f: It serves the southern half of Huvadhu Atoll.

q.q: Which is the last of the 24 basic Thaana letters?
q.f: The 24 letters run from haa to chaviyani.

q.q: Which letter comes third in the Thaana alphabet?
q.f: Noonu Atoll takes its name from this letter.

q.q: How many vowel signs (fili) does Thaana have, not counting the sukun?
q.f: Each short vowel has a long partner: a and aa, i and ee, u and oo, e and ey, o and oa.

q.q: What is the Dhivehi word for 'moon'?
q.f: The sun is 'iru' and a star is 'thari'.

q.q: What is the number 'seven' in Dhivehi?
q.f: Six, seven, eight: haeh, hatheh, asheh.

q.q: What does 'dhonbe' mean?
q.f: An older sister is 'dhaitha'.

q.q: What does 'miskiy' mean?
q.f: The Old Friday Mosque is called Hukuru Miskiy.

q.q: What does 'magu' mean, as in Majeedhee Magu?
q.f: Majeedhee Magu is the main street of Malé.

q.q: What does 'faru' mean, as in Hanifaru?
q.f: A lagoon is called 'vilu'.

q.q: Dhivehi words to do with religion, like 'miskiy', mostly come from which language?
q.f: Arabic words are often written with the extra dotted Thaana letters.

q.q: The first nine Thaana letters come from Arabic numerals. Where do the next nine come from?
q.f: The remaining letters were added later.

q.q: What does 'ran' mean in Dhivehi?
q.f: Silver is 'rihi'.

q.q: What is the Dhivehi word for 'rain'?
q.f: Most of the year's rain comes with the south-west monsoon.

q.q: What is 'lonumirus'?
a: A paste of chilli and salt
q.f: 'Lonu' means salt and 'mirus' means chilli.

q.q: What does 'kukulhu' mean?
q.f: 'Kukulhu riha' is chicken curry.

q.q: What is a 'boakibaa'?
q.f: Kulhi boakibaa is a spicy, savoury fish cake.

q.q: What are 'hikandhifaiy', used in many Maldivian curries?
q.f: They are often fried with onion at the start of a curry.

q.q: 'Kashikeyo' is the fruit of which plant?
q.f: Screwpine grows well in sandy island soil.

q.q: What is 'falhoa'?
q.f: A mango is 'anbu' and a banana is 'dhonkeyo'.

q.q: Mas huni is most often eaten at which meal?
q.f: It is usually served with roshi and a cup of tea.

q.q: Garudhiya is tuna cooked in water with what?
q.f: Boiled down for hours, the broth becomes rihaakuru.

q.q: In Dhivehi food names, what does 'foni' mean?
q.f: 'Foni boakibaa' is a sweet cake.

q.q: 'Kiru sai' is tea made with what?
q.f: 'Kiru' means milk, as in 'kaashikiru', coconut milk.

q.q: What is 'handulu'?
q.f: Cooked rice is 'bath'.

q.q: How is tuna made into hard hikimas?
a: It is boiled, smoked and dried in the sun
q.f: Made this way, it keeps for months without a fridge.

q.q: Hanifaru's manta gatherings happen during which monsoon?
q.f: They peak roughly from May to November.

q.q: What is the north-east monsoon called in Dhivehi?
q.f: It brings the drier season, roughly from December to April.

q.q: What do manta rays eat?
q.f: They filter it from the water with their wide mouths.

q.q: Rays, like sharks, have skeletons made of what?
q.f: Cartilage is lighter and more flexible than bone.

q.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
q.f: Its blood is blue.

q.q: Which fast ocean fish, caught off the Maldives, has a tall fin like a sail on its back?
q.f: It can fold its sail down to swim faster.

q.q: Which reef fish can puff itself up into a ball?
q.f: Many pufferfish are also poisonous to eat.

q.q: What decides whether baby sea turtles hatch male or female?
q.f: Warmer nests produce more females.

q.q: Which is the second-largest fish in the world?
q.f: Like the whale shark, it feeds on plankton.

q.q: Maldivian divers often dive in a 'kandu'. What is it?
q.f: Currents in the channels bring food that draws in big fish.

q.q: In Maldivian diving, what is a 'thila'?
a: A reef top that stays under the surface
q.f: A 'giri' is a coral head that reaches close to the surface.

q.q: Many parrotfish sleep inside what at night?
a: A bubble of mucus they make
q.f: The bubble may hide their scent from hunting moray eels.

q.q: Which sea turtle is named for its narrow, pointed beak?
q.f: Hawksbill turtles are critically endangered.

q.q: In which city did the Maldives win the 2008 SAFF Championship final?
q.f: They beat India 1–0 in the final.

q.q: In which city was the 2018 SAFF Championship final, won by the Maldives, played?
q.f: The Maldives beat India 2–1.

q.q: In carrom, how many carrom men does each player have?
q.f: The board starts with 19 pieces: 9 white, 9 black and the red queen.

q.q: In carrom, which colour does the player who breaks usually play?
q.f: The small flat pieces are called carrom men.

q.q: How many players does a futsal team have on the court?
q.f: Futsal uses a smaller, heavier ball that bounces less.

q.q: In volleyball, how many points win a normal set?
q.f: A deciding fifth set goes to 15.

q.q: How long is an Olympic swimming pool?
q.f: Short-course pools are 25 metres long.

q.q: Badminton is named after Badminton House, a country house in which country?
q.f: Badminton House is in Gloucestershire.

q.q: In which sport is the Ashes series played?
q.f: It is played between England and Australia.

q.q: Which is the only country to have played at every men's FIFA World Cup?
q.f: Brazil's national team is nicknamed the Seleção.

q.q: In cricket, what is a 'maiden over'?
a: An over with no runs scored
The first over of a match
An over with a wicket on every ball
An over bowled by a new player
q.f: It is a good result for the bowler.

q.q: Which chess piece is the only one that can jump over other pieces?
q.f: It moves in an L shape.

q.q: Which Maldivian festival marks the birthday of the Prophet Muhammad?
q.f: It is known elsewhere as Mawlid.

q.q: Langiri, a traditional dance by men, is performed with what?
q.f: It grew out of the older thaara performance.

q.q: Traditionally, dhonis were built from the wood of which tree?
q.f: Many newer boats are made from imported timber or fibreglass.

q.q: What is a 'joali'?
a: A seat made of rope or netting
q.f: Joalis are a common sight outside homes and cafés.

q.q: What is an 'undhoali'?
q.f: It hangs from a frame or a tree and rocks gently.

q.q: Who wrote the words of the national anthem, Gaumee Salaam?
q.f: He wrote them in 1948.

q.q: In which year was the first iPhone released?
q.f: It was launched by Apple's Steve Jobs.

q.q: What is the name of the fictional African country in 'Black Panther'?
q.f: Its hero, T'Challa, is also its king.

q.q: Which Harry Potter house has a lion on its crest?
q.f: Slytherin's crest has a snake.

q.q: In 'The Lion King', what is the name of Simba's father?
q.f: Scar is Mufasa's brother.

q.q: Which band sang 'Bohemian Rhapsody'?
q.f: Its singer was Freddie Mercury.

q.q: Which Pixar film is about toys that come to life?
q.f: Its heroes are the cowboy Woody and the spaceman Buzz Lightyear.

q.q: Felivaru, with one of the country's main fish-processing plants, is in which atoll?
q.f: Much of the tuna from the northern atolls is landed there.

q.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
q.f: It comes from the Latin word 'aurum'.

q.q: Which is the smallest planet in our solar system?
q.f: Mercury is also the closest planet to the Sun.

q.q: How many bones are in an adult human body?
q.f: Babies are born with around 300, and some join together as they grow.

q.q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
q.f: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.

q.q: Which element has the chemical symbol 'Na'?
q.f: The symbol comes from its Latin name, natrium.

q.q: What is the capital of Australia?
q.f: Sydney is its largest city.

q.q: What is the highest mountain above sea level?
q.f: It stands on the border of Nepal and China.

q.q: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
q.f: Counting second-language speakers, English is the most widely spoken.

q.q: Who developed the theory of relativity?
q.f: His famous equation is E = mc².

q.q: What is the official administrative capital of Sri Lanka?
q.f: Colombo is the largest city and the main business centre.

q.q: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
q.f: About 78% of the air is nitrogen.

q.q: In which year did people first land on the Moon?
q.f: Neil Armstrong was the first to step onto it.

q.q: What is the atomic number of carbon?
q.f: All known life on Earth is built on carbon.
